question: Between \(0^\circ\) and \(90^\circ\), what is the angle in degrees for which \(\tan x=1\)?
solution: The tangent of \(45^\circ\) equals 1, and there is no second solution in this range because tangent is strictly increasing for \(0^\circ<x<90^\circ\). If the endpoints are included, \(\tan0^\circ=0\) and \(\tan90^\circ\) is undefined. Thus \(x=45^\circ\).

solutionMethods.explanation: For \(0^\circ<x<90^\circ\), represent \(x\) as an acute angle of a right triangle. Tangent is the opposite leg divided by the adjacent leg, so \(\tan x=1\) means the two positive leg lengths are equal. Their opposite angles are equal and sum to \(90^\circ\), giving \(2x=90^\circ\) and \(x=45^\circ\). Conversely, equal legs give \(\tan45^\circ=1\). If the endpoints are included, \(\tan0^\circ=0\) and \(\tan90^\circ\) is undefined. Thus the only answer in degrees is \(45\).
solutionMethods.label: Equal legs in a right triangle

reference.question: Between \(0^\circ\) and \(90^\circ\), what is the angle in degrees for which \(\tan x=1\)?
reference.solution:
Method 1: Recognize the special angle

The tangent of \(45^\circ\) equals 1, and there is no second solution in this range because tangent is strictly increasing for \(0^\circ<x<90^\circ\). If the endpoints are included, \(\tan0^\circ=0\) and \(\tan90^\circ\) is undefined. Thus \(x=45^\circ\).

Method 2: Equal legs in a right triangle

For \(0^\circ<x<90^\circ\), represent \(x\) as an acute angle of a right triangle. Tangent is the opposite leg divided by the adjacent leg, so \(\tan x=1\) means the two positive leg lengths are equal. Their opposite angles are equal and sum to \(90^\circ\), giving \(2x=90^\circ\) and \(x=45^\circ\). Conversely, equal legs give \(\tan45^\circ=1\). If the endpoints are included, \(\tan0^\circ=0\) and \(\tan90^\circ\) is undefined. Thus the only answer in degrees is \(45\).
